name: Italy
summary: Possessing any drug for personal use is an administrative offence (licence/passport suspension, DPR 309/90 art. 75); supply is a crime. Hemp-flower sales banned in 2025. No legal drug-checking framework.
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Personal-use possession is not a crime, so health staff have no duty to report it and are bound by secrecy. Failing to help someone in danger is an offence (c.p. art. 593).
drugChecking: No national legal framework; a few regional outreach projects (e.g. Neutravel, Piedmont) offer checking at events.

lsd.note: Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence (licence/passport suspension 2–12 months; first minor case may get a warning). Supply is a crime.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin and Psilocybe/Conocybe/Stropharia fungi are Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence. Growing or selling is a crime.

dmt.note: Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence (2–12 months document suspension). Ayahuasca and its plants were added to Table I in 2022.

mescaline.note: Mescaline and peyote (Lophophora williamsii) are Table I: personal possession is administrative. San Pedro cacti are not named in the tables.

dox.note: DOM, DOB and DOC are Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence (2–12 months document suspension); supply is a crime.

nbomes.note: 25I-, 25B-, 25C-NBOMe and many analogues are Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence; supply is a crime.

2c-x.note: 2C-B, 2C-I and analogues are Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence (2–12 months document suspension); supply is a crime.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2, 2C-T-7 and 2C-T-21 are listed in Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence; supply is a crime.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT, 5-MeO-MiPT and 5-MeO-DiPT are listed in Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence; supply is a crime.

cannabis.note: Table II: personal possession → 1–3 months document suspension (indicative limit 500 mg THC). Medical use legal. 'Cannabis light' flower sales banned in 2025.

ketamine.note: Table I (also a licensed anaesthetic): non-prescribed personal possession is an administrative offence (2–12 months document suspension). Supply is a crime.

mxe.note: Methoxetamine is Table I (UN-controlled since 2016): personal possession is an administrative offence; supply is a crime.

dxm.note: Sold in pharmacies as cough medicine without prescription (SOP); dextromethorphan is expressly excluded from the drug tables.

nitrous.note: Not a scheduled drug and no national ban on recreational sale (2026), but some towns ban sale or use by local ordinance.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are Table I: personal possession is administrative. ADHD drugs (methylphenidate, lisdexamfetamine) need a special prescription.

mdma.note: Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence (indicative limit 750 mg MDMA); supply is a crime.

cocaine.note: Table I: personal possession is an administrative offence (indicative limit 750 mg cocaine); supply is a crime.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Legal for adults; selling or serving alcohol to under-18s is prohibited (since 2012).

ghb/gbl.note: GHB and GBL are Table IV: personal possession means 1–3 months document suspension. Sodium oxybate (Alcover, Xyrem) is a prescription medicine.

opioids.note: Heroin and other opioids are Table I: personal possession is administrative (heroin indicative limit 250 mg). Prescription opioids are medical-only.

tramadol.note: Prescription opioid listed in the drug tables; non-prescribed personal possession is an administrative offence like other drugs.

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only and listed in Table IV; non-prescribed personal possession means 1–3 months document suspension.

maois.note: Harmine, harmaline, B. caapi and ayahuasca are Table I since 2022: personal possession is administrative. MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only.

ssris.note: Prescription-only medicines; not controlled drugs, so possession itself is not penalised.
